data.narrative:
ideaForge is a public-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector that has raised $50M+ to date. The valuation universe for this company is constrained: the Drones & Autonomous sector contains five identifiable peers, all private, including Joby Aviation, Archer Aviation, Zipline, Nuro, and Elroy Air. No public comparables exist in this narrow segment.

Peer-median valuation analysis was not applicable given insufficient depth in the comparable set. The methodology requires a minimum of three same-stage or adjacent-stage peers with similar valuation tier placement to produce reliable benchmarking; the dataset yielded only two same-stage peers and zero adjacent-stage peers meeting filtration criteria. Expanding to all five sector peers would introduce heterogeneity in stage and business model that would undermine comparability and produce a misleading central estimate.

Without a sufficiently populated peer cohort, triangulation via standard multiples-based approaches cannot be responsibly applied. A rigorous valuation of ideaForge would require either (1) expansion of the comparison universe to include adjacent autonomous systems verticals with adequate public or late-stage private data, (2) DCF analysis grounded in detailed unit economics and market sizing, or (3) explicit acknowledgment that early-stage private capital valuations in this sector remain driven by investor conviction rather than traded market signals. The core uncertainty is the absence of price discovery mechanisms for comparable-stage businesses in this sector.
